title: tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py BLOCKER: 10 tables duplicated between public/tenant_default on this workspace's live bpm_dev/bpm_test (events_ephemeral*, plat_partition_catalog, plat_event_idempotency, plat_correlation_cursor, plat_effect_completion, plat_partition_maintenance_run_log, event_payload_store) -- recurrence of the ISS-0185 shadow-table family, unrelated to this batch's own migrations
summary: While self-reviewing this batch's two new migrations (1150_par06_instance_projections_event_window.sql, 1151_pin02_instance_started_pinned_versions.sql) against `python tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py`, found the tool reports a pre-existing BLOCKER against this workspace's live bpm_dev/bpm_test databases: 10 table names exist in BOTH `public` and `tenant_default` (event_payload_store, events_ephemeral, events_ephemeral_2026_08/09/10, plat_correlation_cursor, plat_effect_completion, plat_event_idempotency, plat_partition_catalog, plat_partition_maintenance_run_log). Confirmed via `git stash` that this BLOCKER is present identically on a clean checkout of this branch (commit 20151a94) BEFORE any of this batch's code/migration changes -- neither of the two new migrations this batch adds references any of the 10 listed tables, and both pass `lint_migration_schema.py` cleanly on their own. This is the same recurring ISS-0185 shadow-table class already documented extensively in docs/anti-patterns.md's Database/Migrations table ("Creating a copy of a business table in BOTH public and tenant_default...") and closed once before as GH-637 (a near-identical 14-table finding from ISS-0101/GBL-136-era cold-start replay) -- this is a fresh recurrence on a different table set (PAR-01..03/ORD-01/ORD-04-era tables: events_ephemeral*, plat_partition_catalog, plat_event_idempotency, plat_correlation_cursor, plat_effect_completion, plat_partition_maintenance_run_log -- none of which existed at GH-637's time), most likely introduced by one of the recent GBL-13x/PAR-0x/ORD-0x migrations creating its table unqualified (no `-- scope: public` header) against a schema that already carried a same-named copy from an earlier pass, or by a non-GBL numeric migration lacking the per-tenant-vs-public dual-creation guard the anti-patterns entry describes.

root_cause.details: Per docs/anti-patterns.md's dual-schema classification entry: any migration that creates an unqualified table name without first classifying it as GLOBAL_REGISTRY (public canonical) / PER_TENANT (tenant_default canonical) / HYBRID risks the migration runner's public+tenant_default two-pass application silently producing two divergent same-named copies. The specific migration(s) responsible for these 10 tables' public-schema copies were not identified in this pass -- this issue's summary documents the SYMPTOM (confirmed pre-existing, not introduced by this batch) so it is not lost; root-cause identification of exactly which migration(s) among the ~15 GBL-13x/1140-1149 numeric migrations applied since GH-637 lack the proper scope header is deferred to whichever run picks this up.

prevention: Run `python tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py` against a freshly-migrated (not long-lived) bpm_test/bpm_dev to confirm whether this is genuinely migration-caused drift vs. an artifact of this specific long-lived workspace database's replay history.

For each of the 10 listed tables, classify as GLOBAL_REGISTRY/PER_TENANT/HYBRID per docs/anti-patterns.md's existing table, then add the appropriate drop migration (extending GBL-134 for global-shadow-in-tenant, or a new GBL-14x for per-tenant-shadow-in-public) the same way GBL-134/135/136/137/138/139/140/141 already did for the prior 28-investigation cluster.

Audit every migration in the 1140-1151 numeric range and any recent GBL-13x file that creates events_ephemeral*, plat_partition_catalog, plat_event_idempotency, plat_correlation_cursor, plat_effect_completion, or plat_partition_maintenance_run_log for a missing `-- scope: public` header or missing current_schema()-scoped existence guard.
